title: A Multi-Level Image Thresholding Algorithm Based on the Power-Law Distribution
content: The grayscale histogram plays an important role in image thresholding. However, this kind of global statistical information always involves noise. And the correlation mode among image pixels is essential to improve the segmentation qualities. This paper proposes a power-law fitting to the grayscale distribution, so that the noise reduction and pixels’ correlations are both considered by a novel multi-thresholding algorithm. The algorithm generalizes the Gaussian mixture model (GMM) and introduces a non-extensive parameter q to flexibly adapt to the segmentation requirements. Experimental results show that, at threshold numbers of 3, 4, and 5, the proposed algorithm achieves significantly higher PSNR (peak signal-to-noise ratio) on the CT images compared with the Kapur algorithm, the Tsallis entropy algorithm, and the self-adaptive Tsallis entropy algorithm (STEA). For images from the same sequence, the optimal q values converge within a narrow range, demonstrating excellent consistency and stability of the proposed algorithm. Furthermore, in terms of PSNR, SSIM (structural similarity index), FSIM (feature similarity index), and MHD (modified Hausdorff distance) metrics, the proposed algorithm outperforms the GMM on most CT images, validating its broad applicability to images presenting long-range correlations and heavy-tailed grayscale distributions.
